S17.01.note: Model name comes from answer provenance; 'AGI' is the fallback name in code. The footer text is built in ProvenanceFooter.tsx and not a fixed label.
steps: Open the Chat tab and send any message.
Wait until the answer stops streaming.
Look at the line under the answer: it shows the provider and model name.
Compare with your own message: your message is not labelled this way and the answer is.
Optional: the action button under the answer is named 'More message actions for <model name>' for screen readers (VoiceOver/TalkBack).
S17.01.where: Chat tab > send a message and let the answer finish > read the line under the answer (provider · model)

S17.02.note: Streaming and markdown rendering are inner behaviour shown in MessageBubble.tsx; no separate control.
steps: Open the Chat tab and send a message that needs a long answer, such as 'Write five paragraphs about rivers'.
Watch the answer area while the reply is produced.
Check that text grows word by word, not all at once.
Check that headings, bold text and lists look formatted when they arrive.
S17.02.where: Chat tab > send a message > watch the answer text appear

S17.03.note: Indicator default accessibility label is 'Generating response'; a turn status label can replace it.
steps: Send a message in the Chat tab.
Before the first words appear, look for the working indicator.
Check that it is shown and disappears or changes when text arrives.
Optional: with a screen reader, the indicator is announced as 'Generating response'.
S17.03.where: Chat tab > send a message > a working indicator appears above the answer

S17.04.note: The chip only shows when the model supports thinking or reasoning text is present; which model does this is not stated in code.
steps: Pick a model that supports reasoning (see the model list) and send a message.
Look above the answer for the thinking chip showing 'Thinking for' and a time.
Tap the chip (screen-reader name 'Show reasoning').
Check that a sheet opens with the reasoning steps.
Tap 'Dismiss reasoning' to close it.
S17.04.where: Chat tab > send a message to a model that supports thinking > tap the thinking chip above the answer labelled 'Show reasoning'

S17.05.needs: a Cloud or tool-enabled account (tools must be available)
S17.05.note: Which tools run depends on the model and account; the code does not state a fixed prompt that triggers tools.
steps: Send a question that makes the assistant use a tool, such as a web search.
When the answer is done, find the tool activity row above or under the answer.
Tap the row to open the tool timeline.
Check each tool name, its status (for example completed or failed) and the result.
Tap a tool step to view its full output (screen-reader name 'View full output for <tool>').
S17.05.where: Chat tab > send a message that uses a tool (for example web search) > tap the tool activity row under the answer

S17.06.note: Marker behaviour depends on whether numeric citations can link; this was not confirmed in a running build.
steps: Ask a question that needs current web information, such as 'What is the latest version of Node.js?'
Wait for the answer; look for small numbered markers in the text.
Tap a marker.
Check that it opens or highlights the matching source (screen-reader name 'Source <number>: <title>').
S17.06.where: Chat tab > ask a question that needs web sources > tap a numbered citation marker in the answer

S17.07.note: While the answer is still running the title reads 'Sources so far'.
steps: Send a question that uses sources (see S17.06) and wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for a row titled 'Sources'.
Tap the row to expand it.
Check that each source shows its title and host name.
Tap a source to open it.
S17.07.where: Chat tab > finished answer that used sources > tap the 'Sources' row under the answer

S17.08.note: Generated-file cards come from metadata in Cloud mode only (MessageBubble.tsx). The visible words on the card were not confirmed.
steps: Switch to Cloud mode and ask the assistant to create a file.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Look for a file card attached to the answer with the file name.
Tap the card to open it, or use its open control (screen-reader name 'Open <session label>').
Check the file name and type on the card.
S17.08.where: Cloud chat > ask for a file (for example a PDF) > tap the file card on the answer

S17.09.note: Card types are Content, Code, Email, Research, Image, Chart and Document; without a preview the card says 'Open to view details'.
steps: Ask for a document, for example 'Write a one-page project plan as a document'.
Wait for the answer; look for a card on the answer with a type label.
Tap the card.
Check that the artifact viewer or panel opens with the content.
Close the viewer and check the card is still there.
S17.09.where: Chat tab > ask for a document or code > tap the artifact card under the answer

S17.10.needs: an account that can generate images
S17.10.note: The exact prompt that triggers image generation is not written in code; the tester must ask for an image in plain words.
steps: Ask the assistant to make an image, for example 'Draw a red bicycle on a beach'.
Wait for the image to appear inside the answer.
Tap the image to open it full screen.
Use 'Save to Photos', 'Copy image' or 'Share image' from its menu.
Check that the image saves or shares and matches the picture on the answer.
S17.10.where: Chat tab > ask for an image > tap the image in the answer (opens full screen) > use 'Save to Photos' or 'Share image'

S17.12.needs: an account that can generate video
S17.12.note: Playback and download controls were not confirmed by label; only the retry control's text was found.
steps: Ask the assistant to make a short video.
Wait for the answer; look for the video inside it.
Press play and check that the controls work.
Look for a download control on the video.
If generation fails, tap 'Retry video generation' and compare the result with the first attempt.
S17.12.where: Chat tab > ask for a video > the video plays inside the answer; if generation fails, tap 'Retry video generation'

labels.text: Opens a provider search. Confirm the place before navigating.

S17.13.note: Cards are shown only in Cloud mode and only when the model returns them; the code does not define a prompt that always produces one.
steps: Switch to Cloud mode.
Ask a question that returns a card, for example a place search or a choice.
Look for the card inside the answer.
Read the caption under a map card: 'Opens a provider search. Confirm the place before navigating.'
Tap a choice or action on the card and check the result.
S17.13.where: Chat tab in Cloud mode > ask for a place or a choice > use the card in the answer

S17.15.note: A copy failure shows a warning icon instead. 'Copy Message' is the same action in the long-press menu.
steps: Open a finished answer.
Tap the copy icon in the row under the answer.
Check that the icon or label changes to 'Copied'.
Paste into the message box or Notes.
Compare the pasted text with the whole answer.
S17.15.where: Under a finished answer > tap the copy icon (screen-reader name 'Copy') > paste somewhere else

S17.17.note: The icon has no visible word; the name is used by screen readers. If speech is unavailable, a reason shows in the control.
steps: Open a finished answer.
Find the speaker icon in the row under the answer.
Tap it.
Listen for the answer being read aloud.
Compare the spoken text with the answer.
S17.17.where: Under a finished answer > tap the speaker icon (screen-reader name 'Read aloud')

S17.18.note: Same button as Read aloud; it changes state.
steps: Start Read aloud on an answer (see S17.17).
While it is speaking, find the same control; its icon changes to a square.
Tap it (name 'Stop reading aloud').
Check that the speech stops at once.
Check that the control returns to the speaker icon.
S17.18.where: Under an answer that is being read aloud > tap the stop icon (screen-reader name 'Stop reading aloud')

S17.19.note: The button is hidden while a reply is still waiting for approval, and disabled while the conversation is streaming.
steps: Open a finished answer with no unsaved edits.
Tap the refresh icon in the row under the answer.
If a warning appears about unsaved edits, read it and choose to continue or cancel.
Wait for a new answer to the same question.
Compare the new answer with the old one and check the page shows '2 / 2' style paging.
S17.19.where: Under a finished answer > tap the refresh icon (screen-reader name 'Regenerate response')

S17.20.needs: a way to make a turn fail (for example going offline)
S17.20.note: The code does not give a fixed way to force a failure; the tester must find one.
steps: Trigger a failed answer (for example by going offline before sending, then reconnecting, or use a turn that fails).
Read the red failure notice under the answer.
Tap 'Retry' in the notice (hint 'Tap to try again').
Wait for the new attempt.
Check the failure notice is replaced by the new answer or a new outcome.
S17.20.where: A failed answer > the red failure notice under the answer > tap 'Retry'

S17.21.note: The button shows only on the latest continuable answer; the cut-off check is in continuableAnswer.ts.
steps: Ask for a very long answer, for example 'Write a 3000-word story'.
When it stops mid-sentence, look below the answer.
Tap 'Continue generating'.
Check that the same answer continues from where it stopped and is not a new answer.
Check the button disappears when the answer is complete.
S17.21.where: A cut-off answer > tap 'Continue generating' under the answer

S17.22.needs: a second model available to the account
S17.22.note: A failure notice may also offer 'Switch model' instead.
steps: Open a finished answer.
Long-press the answer text, or tap the dots button under it.
Tap 'Retry with Another Model' in the list.
Pick a different model in the model picker that opens.
Check that a new answer comes from the new model and the model name under it changes.
S17.22.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Retry with Another Model' (or the dots button 'More message actions for <model>' > 'Retry with Another Model')

S17.26.note: The code offers 'Quote in reply' only (no separate 'revise' control); the quote is only offered when the chat screen wires reply quoting (MessageList.tsx).
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Select Text'.
Select part of the text in the box that opens.
Read the line that shows your selection.
Tap 'Quote in reply' and check the quote appears in the message box.
S17.26.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Select Text' > select words > 'Quote in reply'

S17.28.note: The arrows show no visible words; the names are the screen-reader labels.
steps: Regenerate an answer at least twice (see S17.19).
Find the pager under the answer, showing a count such as '2 / 3'.
Tap the left arrow (screen-reader name 'Previous response') and then the right arrow ('Next response').
Check the answer text changes to each attempt and the count updates.
Check the arrow is disabled at the first and last attempt.
S17.28.where: Under an answer that has more than one attempt > the pager between the copy and read-aloud icons (shows '2 / 3' style)

S17.29.note: The double-tap gesture has no visible label; it is set up in MessageBubble.tsx and not announced to the user.
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Good Response'.
Check the menu now offers 'Remove Good Response' for that answer.
Close and reopen the menu to confirm the state is kept.
Optional: double-tap the answer text; it also records a good response.
S17.29.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Good Response'; or double-tap the answer

S17.30.note: Whether a detail sheet opens after a bad response (ResponseRatingDetails.tsx) was not checked in this item.
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Bad Response'.
Check the menu now offers 'Remove Bad Response' for that answer.
Reopen the menu and check the state is kept.
Compare with the good response state: only one should be chosen at a time.

S17.31.note: The menu label is written with a unicode ellipsis in code; the tester sees 'Report…'.
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it.
Tap 'Report…'.
Read the sheet title 'Report this response'.
Choose a category and add a note, then send.
Check the result text, such as 'Report submitted for review' or 'Report saved on this device'.
S17.31.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Report…' > choose a category > send

S17.32.note: A single answer is shared through the export sheet, not a link. The conversation 'Share link' entry is in the chat screen menu; the menu button's visible label was not found.
steps: Open a finished answer and long-press it, then tap 'Export Message…'.
In the sheet, tap 'Share Text' to send the answer as text, or 'Share...' to export as PDF and open the system share sheet.
Check the system share sheet appears with the content.
For the whole conversation, open the chat's menu and tap 'Share link' (menu button not confirmed by label).
Compare the shared content with the answer.
S17.32.where: Long-press a finished answer > 'Export Message…' > 'Share Text' or 'Share...'; for the whole chat: chat menu > 'Share link'

S17.35.needs: a finished assistant answer with text
S17.35.note: The sheet offers PDF and plain text only; there is no Markdown option in the code.
steps: Sign in and get a finished answer from the assistant that has text in it.
Long-press the answer, or tap the three-dot icon under it (its label starts "More message actions").
Tap "Export Message…" in the menu. A sheet titled "Export Message" opens.
Tap "Export as PDF". A share sheet opens with a PDF of the answer.
Reopen the sheet and tap "Export as Text". Check that a plain text file is offered to share, then compare with Expected.
S17.35.where: Long-press the answer, or tap the "More message actions" icon under it > Export Message… > Export as PDF / Export as Text

S17.36.note: The usage line appears only when the server sent token or duration figures, and the model name appears in the provider line without the word "model".
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a short question and wait until the answer stops streaming.
Look at the small grey line under the answer. It shows a token count and a time, for example "N tokens · 2.3s".
Look at the line below it. It shows the provider and model that answered, separated by " · ".
Compare with Expected. The code shows tokens and time only; no cost figure is shown.
S17.36.where: Sign in > send a message in a chat > wait for the answer to finish > look at the small grey lines under the answer

S17.37.needs: a way to make the provider fail partway through an answer; no button triggers this
S17.37.note: A reference id is appended when the server logged one, and Retry appears only when retry is available for that message.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a prompt that gets a long answer.
If the answer stops partway with an error, the partial text stays on screen.
Look directly under the partial text for a red-tinted box that starts "Response may be incomplete" and includes the provider's error detail.
If the box shows "Retry", tap it and check that the answer is re-run. Compare with Expected.
S17.37.where: Sign in > send a long question in a chat > if the answer stops with a provider error after some text, look under the partial text for the notice "Response may be incomplete" with "Retry"

labels.text: The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons.

S17.38.needs: a model that declines a message; the tester cannot choose this on purpose
S17.38.note: The box shows only when the provider reports a refusal or content filter finish reason, so the tester cannot trigger it with a chosen prompt.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a message that the model is expected to decline.
When the answer shows the refusal, look for the box under it with the shield icon and the words "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons."
Tap "Switch model" to check that it offers another model, or tap "Report" to check that the feedback screen opens.
Compare with Expected: a separate refusal box, not a generic error or a normal answer.
S17.38.where: Sign in > send a message in a chat > if the model declines, look under the answer for the notice "The model declined to finish this response for safety reasons." with "Switch model" and "Report"

S17.39.note: The code shows "Try again" only when nothing arrived; when partial text was kept, the notice has no retry button, while Expected says to offer a retry.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a question that gives a long answer.
While the answer is still streaming, tap the send button, which changes to "Stop generating".
Look under the partial answer for the notice "Response stopped." Kept text stays on screen.
If no text had arrived, tap "Try again" to check that the turn is re-run. Compare with Expected.
S17.39.where: Sign in > send a long question in a chat > tap "Stop generating" while the answer is streaming > look at the answer

labels.text: The model finished without returning a response. Try again.

S17.40.needs: a provider that returns an empty stream; no button triggers this
S17.40.note: The message is set when the stream closes with nothing in it, so the tester needs a provider that returns no output.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Send a message and wait for the turn to end.
If the turn ends with no text, no tool output and no files, look for the box with the text "The model finished without returning a response. Try again."
Tap the box, which is labelled "Tap to try again." for screen readers, and check that the turn is re-run.
Compare with Expected: an explicit message with retry, not an empty bubble.
S17.40.where: Sign in > send a message in a chat > if the model returns nothing, look under the answer area for the notice "The model finished without returning a response. Try again."
